answers.children: Maltese can be good with children when interactions stay gentle. Their small 4-7 lb build and fragile frame make them vulnerable to accidental injury from rough play, and their affectionate yet playful nature leads them to seek attention rather than herd or guard. The breed's devoted companion history means they bond closely but can become overwhelmed easily. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 6/10)
answers.other-pets: Maltese generally get along with other pets thanks to their sociable and charming temperament. As a toy breed originally developed purely for companionship rather than hunting, they lack strong prey drive and show playful curiosity toward housemates. Their small size requires careful supervision around larger animals to avoid injury during boisterous encounters.
answers.exercise: Maltese need 20 to 30 minutes of exercise daily. Short walks or indoor play with toys suit their moderate energy and tiny legs that tire quickly, while insufficient activity leads to boredom and destructive chewing on household items. Their history as lap dogs for nobility means they adapt well to minimal but consistent mental and physical stimulation.
answers.shedding: Maltese shed very little year-round. Their long silky single coat tangles readily and demands frequent brushing to prevent mats, yet the low shedding means minimal loose hair spreads across furniture and floors in a small home. The silky texture holds onto debris less than coarser coats but still requires grooming effort.
answers.hypoallergenic: The Maltese has a long silky coat that sheds very little and produces minimal dander around the home. This low-shedding quality leads many allergy sufferers to consider the breed, yet no breed is genuinely hypoallergenic. Owners still need to maintain frequent grooming to keep loose hair and skin scales from accumulating on furniture and clothing.
answers.training: Maltese prove moderately easy to train. Their intelligence and affectionate desire to please support learning basic commands, yet independence from their ancient companion role and sensitivity to harsh methods can slow progress. Short playful sessions work best for this toy breed rather than repetitive drills.
answers.lifespan: Maltese live 12-15 years. Their small 4-7 lb size and history as a long-established toy breed from Mediterranean origins support this range, while the profile notes moderate health robustness that owners must maintain through attentive care suited to their delicate build and lively personality. The silky coat and adaptable nature further help them thrive indoors over many years when basic needs are met consistently.
answers.size: Maltese reach 4-7 lb and stand 7-9 in tall as adults. This compact build feels like carrying a silky bundle that fits easily in a lap or handbag, reflecting centuries of refinement as a companion for nobility. Their proportions give surprising agility in short bursts despite the fragile frame that demands respect in daily handling.
answers.barking: Maltese bark moderately often. They alert to doorbells and strangers with a sharp yapping voice rooted in their spunky personality, though their original role as devoted lap dogs keeps excessive noise low when settled with familiar people. The charming yet watchful temperament means barking serves more as communication than constant habit.
answers.apartment: Maltese adapt readily to apartment living. Their low energy, small 4-7 lb size and history as companions for confined noble households allow them to settle indoors with minimal space, while moderate barking and short exercise needs fit busy urban routines without demanding large areas or vigorous activity.
answers.first-time: Maltese can suit first-time owners who accept their demands. The breed's high affection and adaptability to small spaces reward attentive novices, yet their proneness to separation anxiety and fragile 4-7 lb build require consistent routines and gentle handling that may challenge beginners unused to toy-breed sensitivities and grooming needs for the long silky coat.
